# Project Governance 4.1.0

This release keeps ongoing work visible in ordinary conversation, improves context selection and
links observed outcomes and costs without turning missing evidence into success.

- Every associated prompt receives compact deterministic task and workflow facts. Progress questions
  can use the current task without a separate model classifier or a repository scan for those facts.
- Changed input within an active native turn receives a new immutable preparation occurrence.
  Duplicate current input replays; returning to earlier text creates a fresh occurrence. All
  occurrences share the original turn's spending family and preserve task and worktree guards.
- Context excerpts preserve decisive source structure, complementary evidence and winning table
  headings/rows. JEV selection still operates on the permitted inventory and retains conservative
  fallback for incomplete or uncertain advice.
- Typed plan references separate definition identity from deterministic progress updates. Required
  content, specification and source freshness remain guarded.
- Outcome capture retains original usage references, incomplete coverage and unresolved acceptance.
  Provider completion and packet delivery do not establish main-model consumption or task success.
- Entry recovery, consultation context, validation ownership and retained JUnit evidence receive
  focused corrections and regression coverage. Native checks retain their own execution authority.

Local qualification passed 1,023 engine, 82 continuity and 69 verifier tests, both typechecks, exact
installed-package proof and 27 conversational cases. Synthetic published-4.0 upgrade and bound
continuation proof passed. The bound arm used two separately authorized live JEV calls. Opus 5.5
at medium effort closed the material review findings. An optional diagnostic-label correction is
deferred; conservative context suppression remains effective.

This is an operator-authorized manual release using the already qualified archive. Hosted CI is
not part of this qualification. Publication does not upgrade projects or alter native conversations.
Actual desktop consumption, existing-chat upgrade continuity in ordinary work, accepted development
outcomes and total token/time savings remain unqualified. Earlier semantic comparisons are
historical, not a new trial of these exact release bytes.

Adoption is deliberate. Coding models remain fixed and delegation remains opt-in. Decision-provider
interchangeability and supplied-image evaluation are planned for 4.2 and are not implemented here.
